name: Software developers
oneLiner: Split in two: the ones who direct agents are thriving; the ones who wrote boilerplate are not.
why: System-level design and trade-off decisions still need a human
The profession absorbed a generational tool change before and refactored around it
threats: PwC classifies software developers as *democratised* — AI takes the expert tasks and leaves simpler work
Entry-level hiring in these occupations is where the Stanford decline shows up
The task-level exposure keeps rising as models get agentic

claims.text: PwC's 2026 Barometer lists software developers among the roles AI democratises: it automates higher-expertise tasks and leaves the role requiring less expertise, with lower barriers to entry and falling wages.
Democratised jobs make up 52% of advertised roles and are growing half as fast as professionalised roles, with 42% slower wage growth since 2021.
Software developers are among the AI-exposed occupations in which 22–25-year-old employment fell sharply.
